title: Introduce KMS residency fallback planner and RBAC elevation limiter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers operating across regions need resilient KMS usage with strict residency guarantees. When preferred regional CMKs are unavailable (maintenance, degraded provider regions, or temporary operator throttles) we must enforce a deterministic, auditable fallback that preserves residency constraints where possible and surfaces policy decisions to operators. Additionally, RBAC v2 paths occasionally allow short-lived elevation churn (race during operator delegation) which can be abused; introduce an elevation limiter to bound concurrent temporary grants and emit telemetry when thresholds are exceeded.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a KMS Residency Fallback Planner: a deterministic policy engine that selects a fallback CMK based on residency intent, last-known-affinity, tiered consent (tenant-level consent, org allowlist), and operator-scoped leases. Planner exposes a narrow API used by the kms-allocator and kms-proxy. 2) Adds RBAC Elevation Limiter: middleware that tracks temporary elevation tokens (operator leases) per-operator and per-tenant window, imposes soft and hard caps, and integrates with the policy decision cache so rollbacks are immediate. 3) Emits structured audit events for planner decisions and limiter actions: decision_id, reason, candidate_keys, operator_lease_id, and policy_fingerprint. 4) Add a dry-run mode and opt-in shadowing to allow operators to test new fallback rules without affecting traffic. 5) Updates Helm chart and installer flags to expose planner tuning knobs and limiter thresholds.

Backwards compatibility and migration: default behavior preserves current allocation strategy; planner is behind a feature flag (kms.residency.planner.enabled=false) by default. Audit events are additive (new event types); no change to existing audit schema fields. RBAC limiter defaults to permissive thresholds matching historical maxima to avoid operational disruption.

Testing and validation: unit tests for planner selection rules, property-based tests for deterministic ordering, integration tests simulating region failover, e2e with private-installer in a two-zone cluster, and load tests to validate limiter scale and memory usage. CI includes a new slow integration job gated to nightly runs.

Checklist:
- [x] Feature flagged planner and limiter
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Helm and private-installer flags
- [x] Audit event docs and examples
- [x] Shadow/dry-run mode for staged rollout
- [x] Linear ticket linked (ENG-4821), support ticket noted (SUP-679)

Risks and mitigations: planner introduces a small deterministic delay (policy evaluation) at allocation time; mitigated by caching decisions for 60s and pre-warming common tenancy keys. Limiter may surface false positives in bursty operator workflows; added a burst window and rate smoothing.

Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag, enable shadowing for 2 weeks, flip planner on for 10% of traffic with automatic rollback on audit-anchored anomaly detection, then gradual ramp to 100%.

Notes: This PR intentionally separates decision logic (planner) from enforcement (kms-proxy) to ease future policy audits and allow replay of decisions for provenance. See docs/security/kms-residency.md for full operator guide.

rbac: add elevation limiter middleware and in-memory counters with prometheus metrics
audit: emit structured decision events and map to existing audit pipeline
helm: expose kms.residency.* and rbac.limiter.* tunables
installer: add flag to private-installer for planner shadow mode
tests: add unit, property-based, and integration tests for failover scenarios

summary: Feature-flagged KMS residency fallback planner and RBAC elevation limiter with audit and observability; designed for staged rollout and low-risk migration.
